answers.answer: The real task-tier floor calculation is in `bt_scheduler_decision_adapter._tier_floor` (and `_tier_for`). Base tier is computed by `bt_agents.start_tier` with architecture flag if complexity is 'extreme' or scope is 'full_system', and router_complexity 'L' if complexity is 'high' or 'extreme' (promoting base tier to at least 1). Large change / full feature scope raises tier to at least 1; medium or high coupling raises tier to at least 1; estimated duration >= 120 minutes raises tier to at least 1, while >= 240 minutes raises tier to `bt_agents.TOP` (tier 2); high risk raises tier to `bt_agents.TOP` (tier 2). Medium risk alone does not force a higher tier (it is omitted from floor elevation rules).

In `bt_scheduler_decision_adapter._candidate_rows`, pool profiles are retrieved from `bt_agents.pool_for`, profile specs from `bt_profiles.load()`, and configured model/effort options from `_route_options` at or above task tier. Candidate route ID is a SHA-256 hash of `{provider, model, profile, effort}` via `candidate_route_id`. Account identity is not simply a provider name; it is an opaque hash `acct:<sha256>` generated by `account_reference(key)`, where key comes from `bt_agents.account_key(profile, provider)` which encodes the profile provider and normalized environment overlay variables (or underlying account selectors).

In `bt_scheduler_quota_preflight.refresh`, profiles in the project pool are grouped by effective account identity using `bt_agents._pool_account_identity` (which inspects provider-specific environment variables/directories like Claude/Codex config dirs) or `(provider, account_key)`. Refresh is not always forced: for subscription providers ('claude', 'codex'), only the first leader profile per group is polled via `bt_subscriptions.poll`, and if total groups exceed `maximum_accounts` (default 32), polling is bypassed entirely returning `preflight_account_limit_exceeded`. The work is bounded by `maximum_accounts = 32` and polling single representative profile IDs.

Hard eligibility filters are implemented in `bt_scheduler_decision.policy._candidate_reasons` and evaluated in `rank_candidates`. Exclusions are triggered if `not profile_authorized`, `source_status != 'available'`, blocking source reasons, `auth_status != 'valid'`, `runtime_status != 'available'`, or `quota_status != 'available'` (flagging `quota_stale`, `quota_exhausted`, or `quota_unknown`). A good quality score cannot bypass them because `rank_with_route_policy` runs `rank_candidates` first, and only candidates in `ranking.eligible` that pass every hard filter are evaluated by policy objectives.

Quality ranks routes only when `_quality_objective_is_comparable` returns true. Each route requires a valid `ContextualHistoryAssessment` with `minimum_verified_samples >= policy.minimum_verified_samples`, containing exactly one `PerformanceMeasurement` at `selected_level` with `source_quality == 'observed'`, verified sample count >= policy minimum, verified successes + failures == samples, and a valid 95% uncertainty interval in [0, 1]. All eligible routes must have valid intervals and share the exact same `selected_level` (`len(selected_levels) == 1`). If comparable, ranking uses `(0, -quality_lower, quality_upper - quality_lower)`; otherwise quality key falls back to `(0, 0.0, 0.0)`.

When quality is not comparable, the quality tuple is `(0, 0.0, 0.0)`. The lexicographic sort key in `_route_objective_key` then evaluates: (1) quota pressure (`max(window.used_percent)` or candidate `quota_used_percent`, else `math.inf`); (2) duration (`evidence.duration_seconds`, candidate history median duration, else `math.inf`); (3) `relative_cost` if cost is comparable across all candidates sharing single scale, else `math.inf`; (4) `evidence.reserved_for_higher_risk`; (5) `not reset_soon`; (6) `candidate.baseline_rank is None`; (7) baseline rank integer value (default 0); (8) stable `candidate.route_id`. Missing/incomparable duration or cost values default to `math.inf`, demoting them behind known finite values.

No. While `RoutePolicyEvidence` policy capability supports `quality_assessment: ContextualHistoryAssessment | None` and `relative_cost: float | None` (with `relative_cost_scale`), the actual whole-plan adapter in `bt_scheduler_plan_routing._route_evidence` only constructs `RoutePolicyEvidence(quota_windows=windows, duration_seconds=duration)` from local candidate quota and median history duration. It never populates `quality_assessment`, `relative_cost`, or `relative_cost_scale` (leaving them as default `None`), meaning contextual quality and API cost ranking are unwired at the whole-plan adapter level.

In `bt_scheduler_decision.batch._rank_batch_routes`, candidates for each task are grouped by `account_ref` taking the best route per account (`account_options.setdefault(candidate.account_ref, ...)`). Capacity per effective account is clamped to remaining concurrent slots (`max_concurrent - active_assignments`). Two profile aliases sharing one `account_ref` cannot manufacture capacity because matching tracks `occupants_by_account[account_ref]` against `capacity_by_account[account_ref]`. A persisted batch is not a durable execution reservation: docstrings and architecture explicitly state it selects a deterministic assignment set without creating durable reservations (`reservations_created: False`).

Floor variation is tested in `tests/test_scheduler_decision_sources.py` (`test_tier_floor_uses_task_kind_and_classification_rules_without_medium_risk_promotion` and `test_tier_floor_explanation_names_classifications_and_rules_that_raise_it`). Account alias capacity and deduplication are tested in `bt_scheduler_decision/tests/test_batch.py` (`test_shared_account_capacity_counts_active_work_and_profile_aliases_once`). Runtime facts about live account quotas (e.g. real-time rate limits, live token usage, and external provider reset counters) cannot be proven by this static repository snapshot and require querying live provider endpoints or local state caches.

unknowns: Live provider quota balances, reset epochs, and real-time concurrency limits for external accounts not captured in static mock fixtures.
